sentences.text: Synauchenia coalescens was a trout-sized, highly compressed arthrodire placoderm.
Its head shield and trunk shield were fused into an immobile, helmet-like unit because the articulations between the cranium and thorax were lost, leaving no neck gap.
The skull of the holotype — the specimen the species is based on — measures 10 cm in length.
The genus Synauchenia was originally described by Jaekel in 1919, though the only known species, S. coalescens, was formally named by Gross in 1932.
Synosteus, described by Jaekel in 1926, is a synonym for Synauchenia.
Synauchenia belongs to the class Placodermi and is classified within the family Brachydeiridae.
The parent group of Synauchenia is Titanichthyidae, a classification supported by the Paleobi Database.
Fossils of Synauchenia date to the Late Frasnian period, when the animal lived between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago.
This species is found exclusively in the Late Frasnian Kellwasserkalk Fauna of Bad Wildungen.
